# DamIT Processing algorithms (generated: do not edit)

_Generated by `lumo/tools/dump_damit_algorithm_help.py` from the plugin code in an offscreen QGIS. These are the REAL algorithm ids and parameter names. A tool or switch that is not on this page does not exist: never invent one (`damit_runner`, `--no-refine` and `damit_screener_handoff` do not exist). Run one with `qgis_process run <id> --PARAM=value`; an enum parameter takes the 0-based index of its option; a boolean takes 1 or 0 (e.g. `--GRID_REFINE=0`)._

Algorithm ids: `damit_screen:breachdirection`, `damit_screen:engine2d`, `damit_screen:handoff`, `damit_screen:hydrograph`, `damit_screen:preflight`, `damit_screen:prepare`, `damit_screen:report`, `damit_screen:runchain`, `damit_screen:storage`, `damit_screen:suggest`, `damit_screen:terrain`, `damit_screen:triage`, `damit_run:checkhandoff`, `damit_run:hecrasexport`, `damit_run:rundam`, `damit:classify`, `damit_lite:classify`, `damit_data:download`, `damit_data:status`, `damit_pmp:anugarain`, `damit_pmp:basinpf`, `damit_pmp:fetchgrid`, `damit_pmp:gridbasin`, `damit_pmp:hyetograph`, `damit_pmp:pointpf`, `damit_pmp:raingrid`

## Provider `damit_screen` - DamIT Screener (package `damit_screener`)

### `damit_screen:breachdirection` - Breach direction

Group: DamIT screening

Breach azimuth from the dam record (breach_azimuth_deg); otherwise estimated as DamSafety Screening does: the dam axis from <work>/dams/<id>/dam_line.geojson, the downstream side from the reservoir point and the terrain along the line, the breach at the lowest downstream toe (else reservoir -> dam point, else the steepest DEM drop at the dam point; low confidence). A gap only when there is nothing to go on.

Presets: FEMA333 = FEMA 333 baseline, USBR = USBR (ACER TM-11), BIA = BIA, NRCS = NRCS, ND = North Dakota (REG_05.2026), NE = Nebraska, NY = New York, VA = Virginia, TX = Texas, ID = Idaho, CO = Colorado, RI = Rhode Island, AZ = Arizona, CA = California, AK = Alaska, AL = Alabama, NC = North Carolina, USACE = USACE (FEMA 333 terminology), TVA = TVA (FEMA 333 tiers)

Suggested classifications only; the engineer of record and the regulating agency make the determination. DamIT Screener 0.3.1 runs a 2D screening flood (the built-in engine in this process, or LISFLOOD-FP with engine2d = lisflood) and downloads larger clips from the USGS 3DEP service; it never starts ANUGA, HEC-RAS or Wine.

| Parameter | Label | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `WORK` | Work folder | file | - | - |
| `DAMS` | Dams (points) | source | - | - |
| `FIELD_MAP` | Dam field map (damit_field=layer_field, comma separated) | string | - | optional |
| `MODE` | Mode | enum | 0 | options: 0=preset; 1=custom |
| `PRESET` | Preset ID (preset mode; see help) | string | - | optional |
| `SCENARIOS` | Scenario IDs (S-codes, comma separated; empty = preset's) | string | - | optional |
| `METHODS` | Method IDs (custom mode, comma separated) | string | - | optional |

| `SETTINGS` | Settings JSON (file path or text); the fields above win where given, the JSON fills the rest | string | - | optional |

Outputs: `COUNT`, `GAPS`

### `damit_screen:engine2d` - 2D screening flood

Group: DamIT screening

Runs the DamSafety Screening tool-7 2D flood for each dam (the built-in finite-volume engine in this process, or LISFLOOD-FP): the dam's hydrograph CSV, else a Froehlich (2008) piping breach from the top of dam (sunny day, no outlet or spillway flow), injected at the downstream toe (searched 5 m to H x (DS slope + 1), 3:1 when the slope is missing, capped at 150 m, side check). Settings JSON: engine2d (builtin | lisflood | off; lisflood = LISFLOOD-FP ACC, lisflood_exe or an installed one, else the built-in engine with a warning), grid_m (20), simh (12), simmax (96), larger_clips (0 first clip only, 1 a fresh USGS 3DEP download for each larger clip, into <work>/dams/<id>/screen_inputs/terrain_3dep/, 2 from local_dem), timeout_s (0 = 0.8 x DAMIT_SCREENING_TIMEOUT_S, else 3600; the download counts). Writes Screening Depth / Velocity / DV (Max) and Screening Arrival Time into <work>/dams/<id>/ and samples peak depth, velocity and DV at the receptors. ANUGA, HEC-RAS and Wine are not started.

Presets: FEMA333 = FEMA 333 baseline, USBR = USBR (ACER TM-11), BIA = BIA, NRCS = NRCS, ND = North Dakota (REG_05.2026), NE = Nebraska, NY = New York, VA = Virginia, TX = Texas, ID = Idaho, CO = Colorado, RI = Rhode Island, AZ = Arizona, CA = California, AK = Alaska, AL = Alabama, NC = North Carolina, USACE = USACE (FEMA 333 terminology), TVA = TVA (FEMA 333 tiers)

Suggested classifications only; the engineer of record and the regulating agency make the determination. DamIT Screener 0.3.1 runs a 2D screening flood (the built-in engine in this process, or LISFLOOD-FP with engine2d = lisflood) and downloads larger clips from the USGS 3DEP service; it never starts ANUGA, HEC-RAS or Wine.

### `damit_screen:preflight` - Preflight check

Group: DamIT screening

Checks, in seconds, what would make the screening fail or silently skip a step: work folder and disk, DamIT Catalog, preset / custom selection and its catalog flags (unverified, secondary, dash -> M13 fallback, scenario unconfirmed), the dams layer and the fields each chosen scenario needs, terrain, and whether the receptor layer carries the fields the enabled methods read. Missing inputs are WARN or FAIL, never passed. damit_screen:runchain refuses to start on a FAIL.

### `damit_screen:prepare` - Prepare dam inventory

Group: DamIT screening

Maps the dam layer's fields onto DamIT dam fields (FIELD_MAP, e.g. dam_id=NIDID,height_ft=MAX_HT) and checks ids, duplicates and numbers. Writes <work>/damit_screen/dams.json.

The dam inventory is the USACE National Inventory of Dams (NID): every dam needs an NID ID (dam_id = the NID ID, e.g. ND00199, or a nid_id field). A DWR-, DUG- or other non-NID id is a problem; only a new / proposed dam (is_new, or new_or_existing = new) or a desk sample (is_sample) may have none, recorded as a gap.

Presets: FEMA333 = FEMA 333 baseline, USBR = USBR (ACER TM-11), BIA = BIA, NRCS = NRCS, ND = North Dakota (REG_05.2026), NE = Nebraska, NY = New York, VA = Virginia, TX = Texas, ID = Idaho, CO = Colorado, RI = Rhode Island, AZ = Arizona, CA = California, AK = Alaska, AL = Alabama, NC = North Carolina, USACE = USACE (FEMA 333 terminology), TVA = TVA (FEMA 333 tiers)

### `damit_screen:runchain` - Run the screening chain (headless)

Group: DamIT screening

Runs the preflight, then every dam (or the dam_ids in the settings) through: prepare, terrain, storage at each selected scenario's pool (S-codes from the preset or your choice), breach direction, hydrograph, triage (M13 presence screen), 2D screening flood (built-in engine, in this process), preliminary suggestion from the catalog when receptor hydraulics exist, and a damit_handoff.json per dam for damit_run:rundam. A preflight FAIL refuses the run.

Presets: FEMA333 = FEMA 333 baseline, USBR = USBR (ACER TM-11), BIA = BIA, NRCS = NRCS, ND = North Dakota (REG_05.2026), NE = Nebraska, NY = New York, VA = Virginia, TX = Texas, ID = Idaho, CO = Colorado, RI = Rhode Island, AZ = Arizona, CA = California, AK = Alaska, AL = Alabama, NC = North Carolina, USACE = USACE (FEMA 333 terminology), TVA = TVA (FEMA 333 tiers)

### `damit_screen:suggest` - Preliminary suggested class

Group: DamIT screening

### `damit_run:rundam` - Run breach model for one dam

Group: DamIT breach runs

Dam breach flood for one dam, the DamSafety Runner's rundam for the DamIT presets. Sunny day: no inflow and no outlet or spillway flow, the reservoir starting at the top of dam. The breach hydrograph comes from METHOD (Froehlich 2008 piping by default, TR-60, the other DamSafety methods, or your CSV). The breach inflow goes in at the lowest ground of the downstream toe band, 5 m to H x (downstream slope + 1) out from the dam line (3:1 when the slope is not known), never more than 150 m from it. LISFLOOD-FP runs on the DEM and the domain grows until the flood no longer leaves it deeper than the edge tolerance (MAX_RUNS, MAX_EXTENT_MI, DURATION_MAX_HR and the wall-clock limits stop it); a coarse wide, shallow flood is run again at 10 m (GRID_REFINE); Models = ANUGA (or FORCE_ANUGA) re-runs the extent on a mesh and its maxima are the results.

LISFLOOD_EXE: empty = an installed LISFLOOD-FP (the provider setting, NDBREACH_LISFLOOD, lisflood on PATH or a usual install place); when none is found the built-in numpy engine runs instead, with a WARNING in the log, run_report.json and ENGINE_FALLBACK / ENGINE_NOTE (as the old ND Breach Runner did); 'builtin' = the built-in engine on request (a screening approximation, NOT LISFLOOD-FP). A path that does not exist is an error, not a fallback. HEC-RAS 2D is not run by DamIT (choosing it is refused). DamIT never starts HEC-RAS or Wine, and never calls the ND suite's breach runner or batch tools.

The run goes into a NEW folder under OUTPUT_FOLDER (never an existing one): run_setup.json, run_report.json, model/ and outputs/ (Depth (Max).tif ft, Velocity (Max).tif ft/s, WSE (Max).tif ft, Arrival Time.tif h, hmax_ft.tif and the QA rasters, Flood Polygons (Max Depth), Flood Extent, Arrival Zones). With DAMS_FOLDER the rasters and vectors are also copied into <DAMS_FOLDER>/<DAM_ID>/, and an empty height, storage, top of dam or area is read from its dam.json (the dam line, reservoir point and breach point too). Classification is DamIT Hazard's job (damit:classify). DRY_RUN on: prepare and record only (the 0.1.0 behaviour).

NID dams only: the dam's id is its NID ID (National Inventory of Dams, e.g. ND00199), as dam_id or nid_id. A DWR-, DUG- or other non-NID id is refused; a new / proposed dam (IS_NEW) or a desk sample (IS_SAMPLE) may have none, with a warning.

## Provider `damit` - DamIT Hazard (package `damit_hazard`)

### `damit:classify` - Classify dam hazard (preset or custom methods)

Group: 

Suggests a dam hazard class from EXISTING depth / velocity rasters and receptor layers, with a jurisdiction preset (scenarios, methods, parameters and labels from the DamIT Catalog plugin) or with methods you tick (custom: generic labels). Pick the preset from the list or type its ID in 'Preset ID' (an alias such as USBR_TM11 for USBR works too; it wins over the list). It does not run a breach or flood model.<br><br>Rule-strength results set the suggestion; advisory results are listed beside it and count only when 'Apply advisory results' is on. Missing inputs are flagged in the report, never passed silently.<br><br>NID dams only: the dam record (DAM_JSON) names the dam by its NID ID (USACE National Inventory of Dams, e.g. ND00199) as dam_id or nid_id. A DWR-, DUG- or other non-NID id fails; only a new / proposed dam (is_new) or a desk sample (is_sample) may have none, with a warning. The record may be flat or a dam.json with nested "fields"; with no DAM_JSON, the dam.json above the depth raster (or the run watcher's dam_record_hazard.json for that run) is used when it has a dam id, and the report names it.<br><br>Receptor attributes are read by name (type, occupants, floor_elev / floor_height_ft, aadt, road_class, func_class, sole_access, trains_per_day, passenger, ...): see the plugin README.<br><br>Informational screening aid, not a regulatory determination: the engineer of record and the regulating agency make the determination.

## Provider `damit_pmp` - DamIT PMP (NOAA Atlas 14) (package `damit_pmp`)

### `damit_pmp:anugarain` - ANUGA rain-on-grid job on the runner's gmsh mesh

Group: NOAA Atlas 14

Builds an ANUGA rain-on-grid job the way damit_runner builds its ANUGA gmsh model: the runner's own gmsh_mesher.py (a verbatim, sha-pinned copy) meshes a basin polygon or an extent over a DEM with the runner's sizing defaults (lines 100 m2, flow path 250 m2, far field 20000 m2, quality gate min angle 20 deg), the outer ring comes from the runner's terrain.mask_outline, the refinement line is the runner's steepest-descent flow path from an optional start point, and the generated script builds the ANUGA domain with the runner's worker helpers (local coordinates, zero Geo_reference, every outer edge tagged outflow, DE0, minimum storable height 0.001, Manning n 0.06, dry start, edge_bc outflow | transmissive, ground from the model DEM at the centroids or, for a finer DEM, the native DEM at the vertices). The rain is an anuga.Rate_operator (m/s) from the *_anuga_rate.csv of damit_pmp:raingrid, with an optional per-triangle factor sampled from the raingrid FACTOR_RASTER.

Output folder: gmsh_mesh_in.json (mesher input), gmsh_mesh.npz + gmsh_mesh.msh + mesh_triangles.geojson (when the mesh is built), anuga_rain_job.npz, run_anuga_rain.py with the runner files it imports, and run_manifest.json (settings, versions, sha256 of every file). Run the script in the ANUGA Python: `python run_anuga_rain.py --dry` builds the domain and rate operator and checks the storm volume without evolving; `--run` simulates.

Nothing is launched by default. Give an ANUGA Python to build the gmsh mesh here (BUILD_MESH; gmsh only, the runner's launcher with a timeout); RUN_ANUGA (off by default) also runs the full simulation. The runner's worker has no rain: only its mesher, outer ring, flow path, sizes and domain build are reused. Source: NOAA Atlas 14 only (NOAA/NWS Precipitation Frequency Data Server, https://hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/pfds/). Atlas 14 gives precipitation-frequency estimates up to the 1000-year ARI; it is not a PMP study, and DamIT PMP uses no other precipitation source. A location outside Atlas 14 coverage fails with a message.

| Parameter | Label | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DEM` | DEM (projected CRS in metres) | raster | - | - |
| `BASIN` | Basin / domain polygon (the model domain; or use the extent) | source | - | optional |
| `EXTENT` | ... or a rectangular domain (used when no basin is given) | extent | - | optional |
| `RATE_CSV` | Rain series (the *_anuga_rate.csv from damit_pmp:raingrid: time_s, rate_m_per_s) | file | - | - |
| `FACTOR_RASTER` | Spatial rain factor raster (damit_pmp:raingrid FACTOR_RASTER; empty = uniform rain) | raster | - | optional |
| `FLOW_PATH_START` | Flow-path start for the refinement line (like the runner's inflow point; empty = no refinement, a uniform mesh) | point | - | optional |
| `CELL_M` | Model cell size of the DEM grid (m; the runner's CELL default is 10) | number | 10 | - |
| `SIM_TIME_H` | Simulation time (hours; 0 = end of the rain series + 6 h) | number | 0 | - |
| `YIELDSTEP_S` | Yield step (s; runner default 300) | number | 300 | - |
| `EDGE_BC` | Outer boundary (runner edge_bc) | enum | 0 | options: 0=outflow; 1=transmissive |
| `MANNING_N` | Manning n (runner default 0.06) | number | 0.06 | - |
| `ALGORITHM` | ANUGA flow algorithm (runner default DE0) | enum | 0 | advanced; options: 0=DE0; 1=DE1; 2=DE2 |
| `MAX_AREA_M2` | Far-field triangle area (m2; empty = the runner's 20000) | number | - | optional; advanced |
| `LINE_MIN_AREA_M2` | Smallest triangle on the flow path (m2; empty = the runner's 100) | number | - | optional; advanced |
| `GRADE_DIST_M` | Distance over which the size grows to the far field (m; empty = the runner's 1500) | number | - | optional; advanced |
| `BUFFER_M` | Grow the domain by this much (m; the runner buffers its flood footprint by 500, a basin needs none) | number | 0 | advanced |
| `FINE_ELEVATION` | Sample the native DEM at the triangle vertices when it is finer than the cell (the runner's 'fine' elevation) | boolean | True | advanced |
| `THREADS` | Mesher / ANUGA threads (0 = automatic) | number | 1 | advanced |
| `ANUGA_PYTHON` | ANUGA Python interpreter (a path, as in DamSafety Setup; empty = write the job only, launch nothing) | string | - | optional |
| `BUILD_MESH` | Build the gmsh mesh now with the runner's mesher (needs the ANUGA Python above) | boolean | True | - |
| `RUN_ANUGA` | Also RUN the ANUGA simulation (default off; needs the mesh) | boolean | False | - |
| `MESH_TIMEOUT_S` | Mesher wall-clock timeout (s; runner 600) | number | 600 | advanced |
| `RUN_TIMEOUT_H` | ANUGA run wall-clock timeout (hours) | number | 24 | advanced |
| `OUTPUT_DIR` | Output folder | folderDestination | - | - |

Outputs: `OUTPUT_DIR`, `SCRIPT`, `MESH`, `MANIFEST`, `TRIANGLES`

### `damit_pmp:basinpf` - Atlas 14 estimates for a basin (sampled points)

Group: NOAA Atlas 14

Queries PFDS at a point on the basin and up to MAX_POINTS - 1 evenly spread points inside it (one polite request per second, answers cached) and combines the Atlas 14 tables cell by cell (mean or max). Point estimates are not areally reduced: Atlas 14 publishes point values only. For a basin mean over the Atlas 14 grid use damit_pmp:gridbasin with a downloaded Atlas 14 grid. Source: NOAA Atlas 14 only (NOAA/NWS Precipitation Frequency Data Server, https://hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/pfds/). Atlas 14 gives precipitation-frequency estimates up to the 1000-year ARI; it is not a PMP study, and DamIT PMP uses no other precipitation source. A location outside Atlas 14 coverage fails with a message.

| Parameter | Label | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BASIN` | Basin (polygons; all features together) | source | - | - |
| `MAX_POINTS` | Sample points (max) | number | 9 | - |
| `COMBINE` | Combine | enum | 0 | options: 0=mean; 1=max |
| `SERIES` | Series (pds = partial duration / ARI, ams = annual maximum / AEP) | enum | 0 | options: 0=pds; 1=ams |
| `UNITS` | Units | enum | 0 | options: 0=english; 1=metric |
| `DATA` | Estimate | enum | 0 | options: 0=depth; 1=intensity |
| `CACHE_DIR` | PFDS answer cache folder (empty = DamIT pfds_cache setting or next to the outputs) | file | - | optional |
| `OFFLINE` | Offline (cached answers only) | boolean | False | - |
| `OUTPUT_CSV` | Table (CSV) | fileDestination | - | - |
| `OUTPUT_JSON` | Estimates and sources (JSON) | fileDestination | - | - |
| `POINTS` | Sample points | sink | - | optional |

Outputs: `OUTPUT_CSV`, `OUTPUT_JSON`, `POINTS`, `VOLUME`, `DEPTH_100YR_24HR`

### `damit_pmp:fetchgrid` - Fetch an Atlas 14 precipitation-frequency grid (GIS format)

Group: NOAA Atlas 14

Downloads the NOAA Atlas 14 'PF in GIS format' grid for one frequency and duration from the PFDS GIS data source (https://hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/pub/hdsc/data/<region>/<region><ARI>yr<dur><a|al|au>[_ams].zip, the same files as https://hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/pfds/pfds_gis.html), clips it to the point buffer, extent or basin you give, and writes a GeoTIFF in INCHES (NOAA's integer thousandths of an inch x 0.001; Float32, NAD83 geographic, nodata -9999) plus a JSON sidecar (<tif>.json) with the source URL, fetch time, SHA-256, Atlas 14 volume and citation. Choose any of the 10 ARIs (PDS) or 9 AEPs (AMS), any of the 19 durations, and the estimate or its 90% lower / upper bound. The region comes from the point / extent (via a PFDS point query) unless you choose it. Without a clip area the whole regional grid (about 25 MB of cells) is written. Downloads (3-4 MB zips) are cached; OFFLINE uses the cache only. Outside Atlas 14 coverage, or for a file NOAA does not publish, it stops with a message. Source: NOAA Atlas 14 only (NOAA/NWS Precipitation Frequency Data Server, https://hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/pfds/). Atlas 14 gives precipitation-frequency estimates up to the 1000-year ARI; it is not a PMP study, and DamIT PMP uses no other precipitation source. A location outside Atlas 14 coverage fails with a message.

| Parameter | Label | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POINT` | Point (finds the region; clipped to a buffer when no extent or basin is given) | point | - | optional |
| `EXTENT` | Clip extent | extent | - | optional |
| `BASIN` | Clip to basin (polygons) | source | - | optional |
| `MASK_TO_BASIN` | Blank cells outside the basin polygons | boolean | False | - |
| `BUFFER_KM` | Buffer around the point (km) | number | 5 | - |
| `REGION` | Atlas 14 volume folder (Auto = from the point / extent, asks PFDS) | enum | 0 | options: 0=Auto (from the point / extent, via PFDS); 1=sw: Volume 6 (and 1 v5) - Southwest: California, Arizona, Nevada, Utah, New Mexico (current grids); 2=mw: Volume 8 - Midwestern States (includes North Dakota); 3=orb: Volume 2 - Ohio River Basin and surrounding states; 4=se: Volume 9 - Southeastern States; 5=ne: Volume 10 - Northeastern States; 6=tx: Volume 11 - Texas; 7=inw: Volume 12 - Interior Northwest; 8=ak: Volume 7 - Alaska; 9=hi: Volume 4 - Hawaiian Islands; 10=pr: Volume 3 - Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands; 11=sa: Volume 1 (v4, legacy) - Semiarid Southwest, older version 4 grid (PFDS serves v5 under sw) |
| `SERIES` | Series (pds = partial duration / ARI, ams = annual maximum / AEP) | enum | 0 | options: 0=pds; 1=ams |
| `FREQUENCY` | Frequency in years (ARI for PDS: 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000; 1/AEP for AMS: 2 ... 1000) | number | 100 | - |
| `DURATION` | Duration (the 19 Atlas 14 durations, 5 minutes - 60 days) | enum | 9 | options: 0=5-min; 1=10-min; 2=15-min; 3=30-min; 4=60-min; 5=2-hr; 6=3-hr; 7=6-hr; 8=12-hr; 9=24-hr; 10=2-day; 11=3-day; 12=4-day; 13=7-day; 14=10-day; 15=20-day; 16=30-day; 17=45-day; 18=60-day |
| `BOUND` | Estimate or 90% confidence bound | enum | 0 | options: 0=Estimate; 1=Lower 90% confidence limit; 2=Upper 90% confidence limit |
| `CACHE_DIR` | Download cache folder (empty = DamIT pfds_cache setting or next to the output) | file | - | optional |
| `OFFLINE` | Offline (cached downloads / PFDS answers only) | boolean | False | - |
| `OUTPUT` | Atlas 14 grid (GeoTIFF, inches) | rasterDestination | - | - |
| `OUTPUT_JSON` | Source record (JSON; default <GeoTIFF>.json) | fileDestination | - | optional |

Outputs: `OUTPUT`, `OUTPUT_JSON`, `MEAN`, `POINT_VALUE`, `URL`

### `damit_pmp:gridbasin` - Basin statistics of an Atlas 14 grid

Group: NOAA Atlas 14

Mean, minimum and maximum of a NOAA Atlas 14 GIS grid over the basin. Give a grid you have (NOAA's file, values in thousandths of an inch, SCALE 0.001; the frequency and duration are read from the standard file name, e.g. mw100yr24ha.asc, or a damit_pmp:fetchgrid GeoTIFF, already in inches) OR leave GRID empty and choose the frequency, duration, series, bound and region (as in damit_pmp:fetchgrid): the tool then fetches the NOAA grid itself (cached) and reports the basin statistics. The basin is a polygon you supply; Atlas 14 values are point estimates (no areal reduction). Source: NOAA Atlas 14 only (NOAA/NWS Precipitation Frequency Data Server, https://hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/pfds/). Atlas 14 gives precipitation-frequency estimates up to the 1000-year ARI; it is not a PMP study, and DamIT PMP uses no other precipitation source. A location outside Atlas 14 coverage fails with a message.

| Parameter | Label | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GRID` | NOAA Atlas 14 grid (empty = fetch from NOAA with the choices below) | raster | - | optional |
| `BASIN` | Basin (polygons) | source | - | - |
| `SCALE` | Grid value to inches (NOAA files 0.001; fetchgrid GeoTIFFs are read as 1) | number | 0.001 | - |
| `REGION` | Atlas 14 volume folder (Auto = from the point / extent, asks PFDS) | enum | 0 | options: 0=Auto (from the point / extent, via PFDS); 1=sw: Volume 6 (and 1 v5) - Southwest: California, Arizona, Nevada, Utah, New Mexico (current grids); 2=mw: Volume 8 - Midwestern States (includes North Dakota); 3=orb: Volume 2 - Ohio River Basin and surrounding states; 4=se: Volume 9 - Southeastern States; 5=ne: Volume 10 - Northeastern States; 6=tx: Volume 11 - Texas; 7=inw: Volume 12 - Interior Northwest; 8=ak: Volume 7 - Alaska; 9=hi: Volume 4 - Hawaiian Islands; 10=pr: Volume 3 - Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands; 11=sa: Volume 1 (v4, legacy) - Semiarid Southwest, older version 4 grid (PFDS serves v5 under sw) |
| `SERIES` | Series (pds = partial duration / ARI, ams = annual maximum / AEP) | enum | 0 | options: 0=pds; 1=ams |
| `FREQUENCY` | Frequency in years (ARI for PDS: 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000; 1/AEP for AMS: 2 ... 1000) | number | 100 | - |
| `DURATION` | Duration (the 19 Atlas 14 durations, 5 minutes - 60 days) | enum | 9 | options: 0=5-min; 1=10-min; 2=15-min; 3=30-min; 4=60-min; 5=2-hr; 6=3-hr; 7=6-hr; 8=12-hr; 9=24-hr; 10=2-day; 11=3-day; 12=4-day; 13=7-day; 14=10-day; 15=20-day; 16=30-day; 17=45-day; 18=60-day |
| `BOUND` | Estimate or 90% confidence bound | enum | 0 | options: 0=Estimate; 1=Lower 90% confidence limit; 2=Upper 90% confidence limit |
| `CACHE_DIR` | Download cache folder (empty = DamIT pfds_cache setting or next to the output) | file | - | optional |
| `OFFLINE` | Offline (cached downloads / PFDS answers only) | boolean | False | - |
| `OUTPUT_JSON` | Statistics (JSON) | fileDestination | - | - |

Outputs: `OUTPUT_JSON`, `MEAN`

### `damit_pmp:hyetograph` - Design hyetograph from Atlas 14 (alternating block)

Group: NOAA Atlas 14

Builds a design hyetograph by the alternating block method from the Atlas 14 depth-duration curve (JSON from damit_pmp:pointpf / :basinpf): storm total = the Atlas 14 depth for the storm duration at the chosen frequency; sub-durations are log-log interpolated between published Atlas 14 durations. Any of the 10 Atlas 14 frequencies and any of the 19 Atlas 14 durations can be chosen (STORM uses the same list and indices as DURATION in fetchgrid / gridbasin); a storm shorter than the time step, or not a whole number of steps, stops with a message saying which STEP_MIN to use. Not an Atlas 14 temporal distribution. Feed the CSV to damit_pmp:raingrid for LISFLOOD-FP / ANUGA rain-on-grid files. Source: NOAA Atlas 14 only (NOAA/NWS Precipitation Frequency Data Server, https://hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/pfds/). Atlas 14 gives precipitation-frequency estimates up to the 1000-year ARI; it is not a PMP study, and DamIT PMP uses no other precipitation source. A location outside Atlas 14 coverage fails with a message.

| Parameter | Label | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `INPUT_JSON` | Atlas 14 estimates (JSON from pointpf / basinpf) | file | - | - |
| `FREQUENCY` | Frequency in years (ARI for PDS: 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000; 1/AEP for AMS: 2 ... 1000) | number | 100 | - |
| `STORM` | Storm duration (the 19 Atlas 14 durations, same list and indices as DURATION in fetchgrid) | enum | 9 | options: 0=5-min; 1=10-min; 2=15-min; 3=30-min; 4=60-min; 5=2-hr; 6=3-hr; 7=6-hr; 8=12-hr; 9=24-hr; 10=2-day; 11=3-day; 12=4-day; 13=7-day; 14=10-day; 15=20-day; 16=30-day; 17=45-day; 18=60-day |
| `STEP_MIN` | Time step (minutes) | number | 60 | - |
| `OUTPUT_CSV` | Hyetograph (CSV) | fileDestination | - | - |

Outputs: `OUTPUT_CSV`, `TOTAL`

### `damit_pmp:pointpf` - Atlas 14 estimates at a point

Group: NOAA Atlas 14

NOAA Atlas 14 precipitation-frequency estimates (19 durations, 5 min - 60 days; PDS 1 - 1000-year ARI or AMS 1/2 - 1/1000 AEP; 90% bounds) at one point, from PFDS. Writes a CSV table and a JSON file with the Atlas 14 volume, version, region and citation. Source: NOAA Atlas 14 only (NOAA/NWS Precipitation Frequency Data Server, https://hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/pfds/). Atlas 14 gives precipitation-frequency estimates up to the 1000-year ARI; it is not a PMP study, and DamIT PMP uses no other precipitation source. A location outside Atlas 14 coverage fails with a message.

| Parameter | Label | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POINT` | Point | point | - | - |
| `SERIES` | Series (pds = partial duration / ARI, ams = annual maximum / AEP) | enum | 0 | options: 0=pds; 1=ams |
| `UNITS` | Units | enum | 0 | options: 0=english; 1=metric |
| `DATA` | Estimate | enum | 0 | options: 0=depth; 1=intensity |
| `CACHE_DIR` | PFDS answer cache folder (empty = DamIT pfds_cache setting or next to the outputs) | file | - | optional |
| `OFFLINE` | Offline (cached answers only) | boolean | False | - |
| `OUTPUT_CSV` | Table (CSV) | fileDestination | - | - |
| `OUTPUT_JSON` | Estimates and source (JSON) | fileDestination | - | - |

Outputs: `OUTPUT_CSV`, `OUTPUT_JSON`, `VOLUME`, `DEPTH_100YR_24HR`

### `damit_pmp:raingrid` - Rain-on-grid files for LISFLOOD-FP and ANUGA

Group: NOAA Atlas 14

Writes the design storm as rain-on-grid input: (a) a LISFLOOD-FP .rain file (spatially uniform rainfall RATE in mm/hr against time, layout of the LISFLOOD-FP manual: comment line, '<n> seconds', then 'rate time' rows; each hyetograph block is held constant, linear interpolation) for the `rainfall` keyword of the .par file; (b) an ANUGA series CSV (time_s, rate_m_per_s; 1 mm/hr = 2.7778e-7 m/s) with a README showing anuga.Rate_operator use; (c) a JSON record with the units, totals and mass check. The storm is a hyetograph CSV from damit_pmp:hyetograph, or built here from a pointpf / basinpf JSON with FREQUENCY (any Atlas 14 ARI / AEP), STORM duration and STEP_MIN. Optionally the storm total is rescaled to an Atlas 14 grid (damit_pmp:fetchgrid output or NOAA file for the SAME frequency and duration) at a point or as the mean over a basin, and a FACTOR_RASTER (grid / reference depth) is written for spatially varying use. The LISFLOOD-FP dynamic-rain NetCDF is not written (its layout could not be verified without the solver; see the README). Nothing is launched. Source: NOAA Atlas 14 only (NOAA/NWS Precipitation Frequency Data Server, https://hdsc.nws.noaa.gov/pfds/). Atlas 14 gives precipitation-frequency estimates up to the 1000-year ARI; it is not a PMP study, and DamIT PMP uses no other precipitation source. A location outside Atlas 14 coverage fails with a message.

| Parameter | Label | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `INPUT_CSV` | Hyetograph (CSV from damit_pmp:hyetograph; empty = build one from the JSON below) | file | - | optional |
| `INPUT_JSON` | Atlas 14 estimates (JSON from pointpf / basinpf; used when no hyetograph CSV is given) | file | - | optional |
| `FREQUENCY` | Frequency in years (ARI for PDS: 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000; 1/AEP for AMS: 2 ... 1000) (JSON route) | number | 100 | - |
| `STORM` | Storm duration (JSON route; the 19 Atlas 14 durations, same indices as DURATION in fetchgrid) | enum | 9 | options: 0=5-min; 1=10-min; 2=15-min; 3=30-min; 4=60-min; 5=2-hr; 6=3-hr; 7=6-hr; 8=12-hr; 9=24-hr; 10=2-day; 11=3-day; 12=4-day; 13=7-day; 14=10-day; 15=20-day; 16=30-day; 17=45-day; 18=60-day |
| `STEP_MIN` | Time step (minutes; JSON route) | number | 60 | - |
| `SCALE_GRID` | Rescale the storm to this Atlas 14 grid (same frequency and duration) | raster | - | optional |
| `SCALE_BASIN` | ... mean over this basin (polygons) | source | - | optional |
| `SCALE_POINT` | ... or value at this point (used when no basin) | point | - | optional |
| `TIME_UNIT` | Time unit written in the .rain file | enum | 0 | options: 0=seconds; 1=hours; 2=days |
| `RAMP_S` | Seconds each block ramps to the next (>= 1) | number | 1 | - |
| `SIM_TIME_H` | Hold 0 mm/hr until this simulation time (hours; 0 = end of storm) | number | 0 | - |
| `OUTPUT_RAIN` | LISFLOOD-FP rainfall file (.rain, mm/hr) | fileDestination | - | - |
| `OUTPUT_ANUGA` | ANUGA rate series (CSV, m/s) | fileDestination | - | - |
| `OUTPUT_JSON` | Record (JSON) | fileDestination | - | - |
| `FACTOR_RASTER` | Spatial factor raster (grid / reference depth) | rasterDestination | - | optional |

Outputs: `OUTPUT_RAIN`, `OUTPUT_ANUGA`, `OUTPUT_JSON`, `FACTOR_RASTER`, `TOTAL_MM`, `PEAK_MM_HR`
